paragraphs: Abba Shaul bar Nash, and some say bar Ramash.

In Niddah 25b he asks how to determine whether a miscarried fetus is male or female, and says to bring a splinter, etc. Rabbah bar Avuha comments on this, “This was taught only from below upwards,” etc. Hyman suggests he may have been one of the late Tannaim and that his words belong to the baraita recited by R”Ch there.

notes.text: ע״ז means on this here, not the tractate Avodah Zarah. The baraita-reciter initials R”Ch remain unresolved. The historical suggestion is Hyman’s, and the fetus-test quotation remains abbreviated.

The saved whole Davidson Niddah 25b scalar explicitly has Abba Shaul bar Nash, alternatively bar Remes, and the smooth splinter test of the fetus. Ramash/Remesh are vocalizations of the supplied unpointed form, not two newly established people. The reciter ר״ח does not occur in that selected scalar; this is not a whole-page absence claim, and Chiyya is not inserted. ע״ז means on this, not Avodah Zarah. The late-Tanna and baraita-placement suggestions remain Hyman's possibilities; the rest of the primary test is not imported into his etc. quotation.

Niddah 25a explicitly introduces Rabbi Chiyya before the examination discussion, which continues on 25b. There Abba Shaul bar Nash is also called bar Remesh. Rav Nachman reports Rabbah bar Avuha’s qualification about moving the splinter from below upwards. Hyman gives the shorter quotation and proposes both Abba Shaul’s date and how his words fit into the baraita.
